transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. 

Um... I hope I'm explaining this the right way, I don't want to come across as difficult or a complainer or anything. I've always been a very dedicated employee. But... well, for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously what's been happening at my job. I do computer support, and... they started this new ticket rotation and these security audits. 

I mean, I know how it might sound to an outsider, and I really don't want to seem unreasonable, but it really seems like those things are being used to build a paper trail against me. I've tried bringing it up politely, and management keeps showing me the system logs and telling me it’s just standard policy. I always try to be cooperative, so I nod and listen to them, but... it's just been very stressful trying to navigate it. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information for why my primary care doctor suggested I come in.
Do you think someone at your job is intentionally trying to harm you or your career?

Oh, um... "harm" is a very strong word. I really don't want to sit here and sound like some sort of disgruntled employee, because I'm really not. I've always prided myself on being a team player and getting along with everyone. 

But... well, regarding my career? Yes, I suppose it does feel intentional. Like I was saying, for over a year now I’ve just been trying to get someone to take this seriously. It really feels like the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being deliberately used to build a paper trail against me to push me out. 

And I know management just keeps showing me the system logs and saying it’s just standard policy for everyone now. And I always just smile and agree with them in the meetings because I really don't want to cause trouble or seem insubordinate. But behind the scenes, it just feels very targeted at me. 

Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound completely unreasonable saying that out loud to you. I just want to do a good job, you know?
Do you think these actions at your job are directed only at you, or could they also be happening to your coworkers?

Well, um... I mean, they say it's happening to everyone. That's what management tells me when they show me the logs, that it's just the new standard policy for the whole department. And I always tell them I understand, because I really do try to see things from their perspective. I don't want to be the one guy who can't adapt to new procedures, you know?

But... well, I guess I haven't really seen it affecting the younger guys on the team the same way. It's hard to explain without sounding like I'm complaining, which I really try not to do. It just seems like my tickets are the ones getting audited the most, and the rotation always seems to hand me the most complicated issues right before the end of the shift. 

I don't know for sure about the others, though. I try to stay focused on my own work and not pry into my coworkers' business. I've always believed in just keeping my head down and doing my job. Do you think I'm overthinking it? I really don't want to be making a mountain out of a molehill here.
Do you think there's any other explanation for why you're being audited and given complicated issues, other than it being intentional?

Well, I mean... I really try to be open-minded about it. I always try to look at things from every angle before I jump to conclusions. I know sometimes people just make mistakes, or maybe the system really is just randomly generating the audits and the ticket assignments. I've thought about that a lot, actually. I don't want to be the kind of person who assumes the worst in people. 

But... I don't know, it's just been going on for over a year now. And I've really tried to get someone to take it seriously, but it just keeps happening. Even when management shows me the logs and insists it's just the new policy, it... well, it still feels like the whole thing is just being used to build a paper trail against me. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm repeating myself. I just... I want to believe there's another explanation, I really do. I try to be a good employee and just go with the flow. Does it sound like I'm being too stubborn about this? I really hope I'm not coming across as paranoid or anything like that.
Do you think these beliefs about your job would change if you were to leave your current position and start working somewhere else?

Oh, wow. Um... that's a really good question. I actually haven't thought about leaving, to be honest. I've always prided myself on being loyal to the company, you know? I really don't like the idea of just quitting when things get a little difficult. I've always tried to be the kind of person who works through problems rather than running away from them. 

But... if I did leave? I mean, I would certainly hope things would be different somewhere else. I really want to believe that if I just put my head down and do good work, I'll be treated fairly. That's all I've ever wanted, really. 

I guess I'm just not sure. I'd like to think a fresh start would fix everything, but... well, I don't know. Do you think leaving is something I should be considering? I really value your professional opinion on this. I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way and not doing anything rash.

Do you think your beliefs about the ticket rotation and security audits being used against you would change if you were presented with clear evidence that they are truly random and not targeted at you?

Well, um... that's a very fair question. And I'd love to say yes, because I really do try to be a reasonable person. I don't want to be difficult or cause trouble. 

But... like I mentioned a little bit ago, management actually has been showing me the logs. They keep pulling them up and saying it’s just the standard policy. And I always smile and thank them for taking the time to explain it, because I want to be respectful and professional. 

But honestly, Doctor, that's kind of why I'm here. For over a year now, I’ve just been trying to get someone to take this seriously. Because even with the logs they show me, and even though they insist it's just policy... I just know the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me. 

I feel terrible saying it out loud to you, because I know it probably sounds like I'm not being a team player. I really don't want you to think I'm just some disgruntled employee looking for things to complain about. Do you think it's okay that I still feel this way, even after they've showed me their evidence? I just want to make sure I'm not completely out of line by bringing this up to you.
